title: Trace the Baseline to Yesterday's Run
scenario: It is 6:18 AM. The third input for this morning is a set of prior-day prices. Nobody typed them in - they came from somewhere, and where they came from is the whole lesson. Trace the baseline before Variance Check leans on it.
input:
Prior-day prices per hub:
ERCOT: 165
SPP: 92
MISO: 78

Provenance: extracted from yesterday's morning brief, which the 7:00 AM run archived to the briefs-archive folder. If yesterday's run had not archived its brief, this baseline would not exist today.
instructions: Read the provenance line carefully - it names the whole loop.

questions.prompt: Where do these prior-day values come from?
questions.explain: The provenance line traces the values to the brief that yesterday's 7:00 AM run archived - a past OUTPUT of this same workflow.

questions.prompt: In automation terms, what IS a baseline?

options.text: A retained past output reused as a reference for comparison
A duplicate copy of today's feed, kept for safety
A governed policy like the thresholds

questions.explain: The values are not measured today and not a rule - they are what the workflow itself produced last run, kept on purpose so today has something to compare against.

questions.prompt: The map shows an edge from Distribution / Archive back to this node. Why is that NOT a circular dependency?

options.text: It is circular - the map has a bug
Because the edge crosses days: yesterday's archive feeds today's run
Because archives are read-only, cycles cannot happen

questions.explain: Re-read the provenance: the archive being read was written by YESTERDAY's run. Within any single morning the flow is one-directional - the backward edge is temporal.

questions.prompt: What must yesterday's run have done for this baseline to exist at all?

options.text: Archived its brief under the retention policy
Computed the same variance we compute today

questions.explain: The input says it plainly: no archive, no baseline. Retention is not bureaucracy - it is what makes tomorrow's comparisons possible.

artifactOnPass.loopShape: temporal - the backward edge crosses days, not a same-run cycle

copilotPrompt: Profile this baseline: where the values originate, what kind of input a baseline is, why the map's backward edge is temporal rather than circular, and what retention it depends on.
successMessage: Baseline traced. When you later archive today's brief, you will be seeding exactly this input for tomorrow.

intro.heading: Before you inspect: the workflow is a loop

sections.title: Yesterday's output, today's input
sections.body: Daily workflows are loops: each run consumes something its previous run produced. The prior-day baseline is the Meridian loop made visible - prices that exist today only because yesterday's run kept them.

sections.title: The one backward edge
sections.body: Every other edge on the map points forward. The edge from Distribution / Archive back to this node looks like a cycle until you notice it crosses midnight. Reading edges temporally is a map-literacy skill.

sections.title: Retention enables comparison
sections.body: vsPriorDay in Variance Check is only computable because a retention rule kept yesterday's brief. When you reach the final lesson and set retentionDays, remember: this input is what that policy protects.

sections.title: Baseline vs template (coming later)
sections.body: Two things carry over from yesterday: this baseline (DATA - the numbers) and the brief template (STRUCTURE - the sections). The Prior Day Brief Template task covers the other one; keeping them distinct matters.

realWorld.soloRebuildPath: You'd look up yesterday's closing values (from your archive or a prior report) and stage them as the baseline this run compares against.

bestFit.how: 'Get items' from the archive library filtered to yesterday's date
a 'Find Record' search step against the archive table, with a fallback if none is found

takeaway.heading: Baseline traced
points: You traced today's comparison numbers to yesterday's archived brief - the workflow consuming its previous self.
You read the map's one backward edge correctly: temporal, not circular.
You connected retention to capability: no archive yesterday means no vsPriorDay today.
In the final lesson you will stand on the other side of this loop, archiving today's brief as tomorrow's baseline.
The workflow can now reuse yesterday's retained output as today's comparison baseline.
